title: Frontend Developer
summary: From your first web request to a deployed React app: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, the DOM, TypeScript, testing and shipping.

nodes.title: How the Web Works
nodes.description: What happens between you and a website: browsers, servers, HTTP and the three languages of the web.

tasks.title: Getting started with the web
tasks.description: MDN's beginner overview: browsers, servers, domains and what a 'page' really is.

tasks.title: How browsers render a page
tasks.description: Watch web.dev's introduction to how browsers turn HTML, CSS and JS into pixels.

tasks.title: Inspect a real page
tasks.description: Open any site, right-click an element and choose Inspect. Find its CSS rules and count how many styles apply.

tasks.title: Web basics check
tasks.description: Three quick questions on how the web works.

questions.prompt: What does a browser send first to fetch a web page?
questions.explanation: The browser sends an HTTP request over a connection; DNS only resolves the name first.

questions.prompt: Which protocol encrypts web traffic in transit?
questions.explanation: HTTPS wraps HTTP in TLS, encrypting the content between browser and server.

questions.prompt: HTML, CSS and JavaScript all run…
questions.explanation: The browser parses HTML, applies CSS and executes JavaScript to render the page.

nodes.title: HTML Foundations
nodes.description: Structure pages with semantic elements: headings, lists, images, links and forms.

tasks.title: The HTML guide
tasks.description: MDN's HTML reference: elements, attributes and document structure.

tasks.title: freeCodeCamp: HTML courses
tasks.description: Work through the HTML lessons on freeCodeCamp's learn path.

tasks.title: Structure a profile page
tasks.description: Build a page with a <header>, a <main> containing two <section>s, an ordered list of skills, and a <figure> with an image and <figcaption>.

tasks.title: Forms: a contact form
tasks.description: Create a form with name, email and message fields. Every input needs a <label>, the email input uses type=email, and the form has a submit button.

tasks.title: HTML quiz
tasks.description: Semantic elements, accessibility and forms.

questions.prompt: Which element best wraps the main unique content of a page?
questions.explanation: <main> is the semantic container for the page's primary content; use one per page.

questions.prompt: Which attribute makes an accessible to screen readers?
questions.explanation: alt text is read by assistive technology and shown when the image fails to load.

questions.prompt: Which input type gets native email validation in the browser?
questions.explanation: type=email makes the browser check the value looks like an address before submitting.

nodes.title: Git & Version Control
nodes.description: Track your work: repositories, commits, branches and your first merge.

tasks.title: Git documentation
tasks.description: The official Git docs: concepts and the everyday commands.

tasks.title: Pro Git (free book)
tasks.description: Skim the first three chapters of the free Pro Git book.

tasks.title: Commit and branch
tasks.description: git init a folder, make three commits, create a feature branch, commit there, then merge it back and explain what happened.

tasks.title: Git quiz
tasks.description: Repositories, commits and branches.

questions.prompt: What does git commit actually store?
options: Only the files changed since the last commit
A snapshot of every tracked file
A zip archive of the repo
questions.explanation: Git is a snapshot tool: each commit records the full state of the tracked files.

questions.prompt: You are on a feature branch and want your default branch's working tree. Which command switches branches?
questions.explanation: git switch (or git checkout) moves your working tree to another branch.

questions.prompt: What is the staging area for?
options: Choosing exactly which changes go into the next commit
questions.explanation: git add places changes in the index, and the next commit captures exactly that selection.

nodes.title: CSS & Layout
nodes.description: Style everything: the box model, typography, Flexbox and the cascade.

tasks.title: The CSS guide
tasks.description: MDN's CSS overview: selectors, the cascade, and how styles apply.

tasks.title: MDN Learn: CSS
tasks.description: Work through the CSS lessons on MDN's Learn path.

tasks.title: Box model & typography
tasks.description: Restyle a paragraph block so content, padding, border and margin are each a different colour. Set a readable line-height and max-width.

tasks.title: Layout with Flexbox
tasks.description: Build a navbar with a logo, three links and a button, spaced with justify-content and align-items — no floats, no absolute positioning.

tasks.title: CSS quiz
tasks.description: Box model, Flexbox and media queries.

questions.prompt: In the box model, which layer sits directly outside the padding?
questions.explanation: Order from the inside out: content → padding → border → margin.

questions.prompt: Which property aligns flex items along the MAIN axis?
questions.explanation: justify-content works on the main axis; align-items works on the cross axis.

questions.prompt: Media queries are used to…
options: Hide the DOM from search engines
Apply styles based on features like viewport width
questions.explanation: @media rules let styles respond to device features — the core of responsive design.

nodes.title: JavaScript Essentials
nodes.description: The language of the web: variables, functions, arrays, objects and promises.

tasks.title: The JavaScript guide
tasks.description: MDN's JavaScript area: the language, the standard library and the Web API.

tasks.title: JavaScript on freeCodeCamp
tasks.description: Complete the JavaScript basics courses on freeCodeCamp.

tasks.title: Variables, functions & loops
tasks.description: Write three small functions: one that sums an array, one that reverses a string, and one that counts the vowels in a sentence. Test each in the console.

tasks.title: Array methods
tasks.description: Given a list of 10 numbers, produce: the evens (filter), their squares (map), and their total (reduce) — chained or separate, your choice.

tasks.title: JavaScript quiz
tasks.description: Five questions on the language core.

questions.prompt: Which keyword declares a block-scoped variable that can be reassigned?
questions.explanation: let is block-scoped and reassignable; var is function-scoped; const cannot be reassigned.

questions.prompt: What does [1, 2, 3].map(n => n * 2) return?
questions.explanation: map builds a new array by applying the function to every element.

questions.prompt: Which of these is NOT a primitive type in JavaScript?
questions.explanation: Primitives are string, number, bigint, boolean, undefined, symbol and null — everything else is an object.

questions.prompt: What is the result of typeof null?
questions.explanation: A famous historical bug: null has been typeof 'object' since the first JavaScript interpreter.

questions.prompt: A Promise represents…
options: A value that will be available later
questions.explanation: Promises model asynchronous results: pending, fulfilled or rejected.

nodes.title: DOM & Events
nodes.description: Make pages interactive: select elements, change them, and react to user events.

tasks.title: The Web API
tasks.description: MDN's Web API reference: the DOM, events, fetch and friends.

tasks.title: Select & style elements
tasks.description: On any HTML page you wrote, use querySelector to select three different elements and change one attribute or style on each.

tasks.title: Make a button counter
tasks.description: A button and a number on a page: clicking increases the number, a second button resets it. No frameworks — plain DOM APIs.

tasks.title: DOM quiz
tasks.description: Selectors, events and element creation.

questions.prompt: Which method finds the first element matching a CSS selector?
questions.explanation: querySelector takes any CSS selector and returns the first match (or null).

questions.prompt: With button.addEventListener('click', fn), when does fn run?
options: When the user clicks the button
questions.explanation: Event listeners fire when the named event happens on the element.

questions.prompt: How do you create a new <div> in code?
questions.explanation: createElement builds the element; you still have to append it to the document.

nodes.title: Responsive Design & Accessibility
nodes.description: Design for every screen: mobile-first CSS, and make your pages work for everyone.

tasks.title: MDN Learn: CSS layout & responsive design
tasks.description: MDN's responsive design lessons, including media queries and the viewport.

tasks.title: web.dev: responsive design guides
tasks.description: Work through Google's responsive design guides on web.dev.

tasks.title: Mobile-first layout
tasks.description: Take one of your pages and rebuild it mobile-first: base styles for 360px, then two media-query breakpoints for tablet and desktop.

tasks.title: Accessibility pass
tasks.description: Audit one page: text contrast ≥ 4.5:1, every input has a label, images have alt text, and everything is reachable by keyboard. Write down what you fixed.

nodes.title: React Fundamentals
nodes.description: Component-driven UIs: props, state, events and thinking in components.

tasks.title: React: Quick Start
tasks.description: The official React docs' getting-started track: components, JSX and rendering.

tasks.title: webdevs: React walkthroughs
tasks.description: Watch a React tutorial from the webdevs channel and follow along.

tasks.title: Components & props
tasks.description: Build a small app from three components: a header, a list of items, and an item row. The parent passes data down through props.

tasks.title: State & events: a todo list
tasks.description: A todo list where you can add items and mark them done. State lives in the parent; updates re-render the list.

tasks.title: React quiz
tasks.description: Components, props, state and hooks.

questions.prompt: In React, the basic building block of the UI is a…
questions.explanation: Components are functions that return UI; you compose apps by nesting them.

questions.prompt: Props in React are…
options: Read-only inputs passed from a parent
questions.explanation: Data flows down: parents pass props to children, and children never mutate them.

questions.prompt: Which hook stores state in a function component?
questions.explanation: useState returns a value and a setter; setting the value schedules a re-render.

questions.prompt: State updates in React are…
questions.explanation: React batches updates and re-renders asynchronously — never assume the UI changed the instant you call the setter.

nodes.title: TypeScript
nodes.description: Add static types to JavaScript: interfaces, generics and catching bugs before runtime.

tasks.title: The TypeScript Handbook
tasks.description: The official handbook's core chapters: types, interfaces and narrowing.

tasks.title: Types, interfaces & generics
tasks.description: Write a typed User interface, a function that filters a list of users by role, and a generic identity function with a constraint.

tasks.title: Port a JS file to TypeScript
tasks.description: Take one of your plain-JS practice files, add types to every function signature, and note which bugs the compiler caught for you.

nodes.title: Testing JavaScript
nodes.description: Write tests that catch regressions: unit tests with Jest and component tests with React Testing Library.

tasks.title: Jest: Getting Started
tasks.description: The official Jest docs: describe/it/expect and running your first test.

tasks.title: Unit test a utility function
tasks.description: Write tests for your sum/reverse/vowels functions (or similar): at least 3 test cases each, including one edge case.

tasks.title: Test a React component
tasks.description: With React Testing Library, render your todo list: type in an item, press add, and assert the item appears.

nodes.title: Build Tools & Bundlers
nodes.description: How modern apps are built: dev servers, HMR, env vars and production bundles with Vite.

tasks.title: The Vite guide
tasks.description: Vite's official guide: how the dev server and the build pipeline work.

tasks.title: Scaffold a Vite project
tasks.description: Create a new Vite + React + TypeScript project, run it locally, and explain in two sentences what HMR just did when you edited a file.

tasks.title: Configure env vars & aliases
tasks.description: Add a .env file with one variable, read it in the app, and set up a path alias (@/) so imports stop using ../../.

nodes.title: Deployment & DevOps Basics
nodes.description: Ship it: static hosting, environment-specific builds, and what happens after you press deploy.

tasks.title: Vercel docs: front-end frameworks
tasks.description: How platforms deploy SPA frameworks: builds, preview URLs and environments.

tasks.title: CI/CD for front-end devs
tasks.description: Watch an introduction to CI/CD and note two things it could do for your workflow.

tasks.title: Ship a live preview
tasks.description: Deploy your todo app to a free host so it has a public URL. Verify the production build (not the dev server) is what runs.

tasks.title: Portfolio v1
tasks.description: A personal site with at least three pages (home, projects, about), built with Vite + React, responsive on 375/768/1280, and deployed to a public URL. Include a short reflection on what was hardest.
